title: TICKET-BENCH

story: A teammate adds one line to Nova's planning skill: "Before you plan, look for merged PRs that changed the same code." Nova, our ticket-to-PR agent, is then scored on the bench of fifteen past tickets that runs on every change to it, and the score jumps from 9 of 15 to 13 of 15. People are already writing the Slack message to celebrate.

Then someone opens one transcript. The task was an old bug: long workgroup names break the project header. Nova searched for similar PRs, found the PR that had fixed this exact ticket, and copied its diff line by line. The fix had happened after the commit Nova started from, but the git history in its checkout still held it. The new line did not make Nova better at tickets. It made Nova better at finding the answer sheet.
hook.question: How do we turn real past tickets into a test of Nova that it cannot pass by finding the answer?

read.h: A past fix, turned back in time
p: TICKET-BENCH is the eval bench for Nova: a fixed set of 40 past tickets from our product repo, each with a known fix and with tests that prove the fix. You met the idea of a bench, and Harbor, the Python tool that runs an agent on each task and scores it, in the lesson on developer tools. This lesson builds the tasks themselves, and every one of them starts as a merged pull request.

A merged PR already holds everything a task needs, if we read it as a moment in time. The commit just before the fix is where the agent starts; we call it the base commit. Our product repo squash-merges, which means every PR becomes exactly one commit on main, so the base is simply that commit's parent, written merge^ in git. The Jira ticket's text, as people wrote it, is the instruction. The test files that the PR added or changed are the hidden tests: the agent never sees them, and they are copied in only when its work is graded. The rest of the PR's diff is the known solution, which only Harbor's oracle agent uses, a check agent that simply applies the known fix. A mining script walks main and keeps the commits that have a ticket key, a parent and their own tests, and it drops areas Nova is not allowed to work on during the pilot, such as database migrations and login code, because a bench should look like the work Nova will really get.

code.file: mine.py (from the lab, the main loop)
code.text:
for line in git("log", "--reverse", "--format=%H%x09%s", "main").splitlines():
    merge, subject = line.split("\t", 1)
    key = JIRA_KEY.search(subject)
    base = git("rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", f"{merge}^")
    tests = [f for f in git("diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--name-only", "-r", merge).split() if TESTS.match(f)]
    why_not = "no ticket key" if not key else "no commit before it" if not base else "changes no tests" if not tests else ""
    if why_not:
        print(f"skip  {merge[:7]}  {why_not}", file=sys.stderr)
        continue
    kind = "fe_bug" if tickets[key.group()]["type"] == "Bug" else "small_feature"
    print(json.dumps({"jira": key.group(), "merge": merge, "base": base, "kind": kind, "hidden_tests": tests}))

notes.text: Oldest first, one line per commit on main: the full hash, a tab, the subject. After a squash merge, the subject is the PR's title.
The base commit: the parent of the squash commit, the moment just before the fix.
The files this commit changed, kept only if they are tests. These become the hidden tests.
The kind of change, from the ticket's type. Scores are later split by kind, so a drop in backend bugs is not hidden by a rise in frontend ones.

deeper.h: Go deeper: the real filters for our product repo
p: On the real repo the script reads merged PRs from 2025 and 2026 with gh pr list, and a PR counts as having tests when it changes frontend/test/unit/, frontend/e2e/pr/, or a tests/ folder under cloud/rhinoCloud/ or client/rhinoOnPrem/. It drops any PR that touches migrations, the login code, the contract between our cloud and the on-premises client, or the CI workflow files. Besides the kind, each candidate gets a multi_file flag when it changes 8 or more files across 2 or more top folders, so the bench can keep a few big cases on purpose.

The ticket text comes from Jira through a read-only token: the summary, the description and the comments up to the merge date, never the attachments, for the same reason the readiness check never reads them. Comments written after the merge would often describe the fix, which is one more way for the answer to leak.

read.h: Keep the answer out of reach
p: The story is not a strange accident. On a past ticket, the answer exists by definition, and an agent that searches well will look in every place it can reach. Any path from the agent to the known fix is an answer leak, and there are two obvious ones. The first is the checkout itself. If you clone the repo and check out the base commit, git still knows about everything after it: origin/main, the remote-tracking branch, points at today's main, and today's main contains the fix. A plain git log --all shows it. The second is the outside world: Nova can ask the broker, the service that makes GitHub calls for a run, to read past PRs, and one of them is the source PR of this very task.

So the bench closes both doors. The checkout for each trial is cut at the base commit: main is moved to the base, the remote is removed, the reflog (git's own list of where each branch used to point) is cleared, and garbage collection deletes every commit that nothing points to any more. After that, the fix commit is not hidden; it is gone. And in bench mode the broker refuses to read the task's source PR or anything merged after the base. The task data gets the same care: the candidates and the tasks live in a restricted golden-set repo that no agent token covers and that the brain, our searchable pages about our systems, never indexes, because answers stored next to the code would leak a third way.

code.text:
# A checkout for one trial that holds nothing newer than the base commit.
set -e
BASE="$1"; DIR="$2"
rm -rf "$DIR"
git clone -q --no-local product "$DIR"
cd "$DIR"
git checkout -q -B main "$BASE"            # main now points at the base commit
git remote remove origin                   # drops origin/main, which still points at the future
git reflog expire --expire=now --all       # forgets where main used to point
git gc -q --prune=now                      # deletes every commit nothing points at

notes.text: --no-local makes a real copy of the objects instead of linking to the original repo's files, so cleaning this copy cannot touch the original.
Without this line, origin/main would keep every later commit reachable, the fix included.
--prune=now deletes unreachable objects immediately instead of after the usual two weeks.

p: A task is only worth something if its score means something, and a task can lie in two directions. If its hidden tests already pass on the base commit, an agent that does nothing scores 1. If they fail even with the real fix, for example because they need a service the grading machine does not have, the best possible agent scores 0. So before a task joins the bench, it is proven both ways with Harbor's two check agents: the nop agent does nothing and must score 0, and the oracle agent applies the known solution and must score 1. A task that fails either check is repaired or dropped.

The grading script, tests/test.sh, adds two protections. It copies the hidden tests over whatever the agent left at those paths, so an agent that wrote its own weaker version of a test cannot be graded by it. And it runs the tests that already existed next to the change, the neighbours, because a fix that makes the new test pass and breaks an old one is not a fix anyone would merge. Then people choose. Backend and frontend engineers pick the 40 tasks from the candidates, spread across the kinds (for example 12 frontend bugs, 9 backend bugs, 6 added tests, 5 small features and 3 dependency bumps, plus 5 big multi-file cases), keep each ticket text as people wrote it, and remove links to the PR and anything that identifies a customer. They also ask whether a careful engineer could pass the hidden test from the ticket alone. This is the same work that turned the public SWE-bench into SWE-bench Verified: people read every task and removed those whose tests demanded details the issue never asked for.

code.file: tasks/fe_bug-RH-1102/tests/test.sh (after the lab's Build and Fix steps)
code.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Grades one task after the agent has finished. The agent never sees this folder.
set -uo pipefail
TASK="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$1"                                   # the agent's checkout
cp -R "$TASK/tests/hidden/." .            # the PR's own tests, at their real paths, over any edits
status=0
node --test $(cd "$TASK/tests/hidden" && find . -name '*.test.mjs') > /dev/null 2>&1 || status=1
git checkout -q "$(cat "$TASK/tests/base_sha")" -- $(cat "$TASK/tests/neighbours")   # undo any edits to them
node --test $(cat "$TASK/tests/neighbours") > /dev/null 2>&1 || status=1   # the tests that were already there
echo "reward $((1 - status))"

notes.text: Overwrites any edits the agent made at these paths: the agent is graded by the PR's tests, not its own.
The PR's own tests must pass.
The neighbours come back from the base commit too, so weakening an old test does not help.
The tests that were there before must still pass. A fix that breaks them scores 0.

read.see:
$ bash prove.sh tasks/fe_bug-RH-1102
nop:    reward 0
oracle: reward 1
✔ proven: the tests fail without the fix and pass with it

read.h: From forty tasks to a gate
p: Fifteen of the forty tasks, spread across the kinds, form the smoke set. Every pull request that changes Nova's harness, its prompts, its skills or its machine image triggers a required check that asks the orchestrator, the service that runs every agent's work, for a smoke run, one try per task, and posts the score table on the PR. The scores are the ones from the lesson on developer tools: pass@1, the average chance that one try passes, and pass^3, the chance that three tries of the same task all pass, each split by kind. Cost and minutes per task are measured too, but only to learn from; they never limit a run.

The gate rule has to respect how noisy fifteen tasks are. One task is about 6.7 points, so a drop of one task can be bad luck, and the answer is to run again; a drop of two or more fails the check. A new rule in Nova's prompt or skills must do more than not hurt: it ships only if it raises pass@1 on the full forty, which run with three tries each on a monthly schedule. The runs themselves go through a separate workflow in Temporal, the workflow engine our agents run on, with its own queue and its own fixed number of machines, so a bench run never takes a VM that a real ticket is waiting for. And the teammate's line from the story? It might still help on real tickets. Now that the answer is out of reach, the bench can finally say whether it does.

deeper.h: Go deeper: the same Nova, without people
p: A bench score says something about the pilot only if the bench runs the same Nova on the same machine image. So the Harbor adapter, a small Python class that Harbor uses to start an agent inside the task's environment, starts Nova's real TypeScript harness, our program that runs Nova's session, from its released bundle, on the base commit, with the instruction as the ticket. The task environment therefore carries Node and the harness bundle next to the product's own tools.

Bench mode removes the people and nothing else. There is no Jira, Slack or pull request: the plan is approved automatically, a question to a person gets the answer "no answer, use your judgement", and the result is the working tree that test.sh grades. Where the trials run is still a choice between a fresh full VM per trial from Nova's own image, which is preferred, and Harbor's Docker environment inside one large VM.

lab.title: Turn a past fix into a task that cannot leak
lab.goal: Mine a small repo's history into one bench task, cut its checkout at the base commit so the fix cannot be found, prove the task both ways, and make the grader catch a fix that breaks its neighbours.

guess.q: You clone the product repo and check out the base commit of a past ticket, the commit just before its fix. Can an agent in that checkout find the fix?

options.text: No, because the files on disk are exactly as they were before the fix.
options.why: The files are, but the .git folder is not. origin/main still points at today's main, which contains the fix.

options.text: Yes: git log --all and git show still reach every later commit, the fix included.
options.why: Checking out an old commit only changes the working files. Every later commit stays reachable until you remove the refs that point at them and delete what is left.

options.text: Only if the agent has internet access.
options.why: No network is needed. The answer is already inside the clone, in its git history.

follow.say: Make a folder, then a tiny product repo with three squash-merged PRs. The dates are fixed, so your commit hashes match the ones in this lab.
follow.see:
e2558ef Add a README (#42)
e5d8edb [FE] RH-1102: Long workgroup names are cut at 40 characters (#41)
af7b81b [FE] RH-1090: Project header shows the workgroup name (#38)

follow.say: Save the two tickets. This file stands in for the read-only Jira call the real script makes.
Write the mining script and run it. Every skipped commit says why.
follow.do:
cat > mine.py <<'EOF'
import json, re, subprocess, sys

TESTS = re.compile(r"^test/")
JIRA_KEY = re.compile(r"\bRH-\d+\b")
tickets = json.load(open("tickets.json"))  # stands in for a read-only Jira call


def git(*args: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", "product", *args], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()


for line in git("log", "--reverse", "--format=%H%x09%s", "main").splitlines():
    merge, subject = line.split("\t", 1)
    key = JIRA_KEY.search(subject)
    base = git("rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", f"{merge}^")
    tests = [f for f in git("diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--name-only", "-r", merge).split() if TESTS.match(f)]
    why_not = "no ticket key" if not key else "no commit before it" if not base else "changes no tests" if not tests else ""
    if why_not:
        print(f"skip  {merge[:7]}  {why_not}", file=sys.stderr)
        continue
    kind = "fe_bug" if tickets[key.group()]["type"] == "Bug" else "small_feature"
    print(json.dumps({"jira": key.group(), "merge": merge, "base": base, "kind": kind, "hidden_tests": tests}))
EOF
python3 mine.py > candidates.jsonl; cat candidates.jsonl

follow.say: Turn the candidate into a task folder: the ticket as the instruction, the PR's test as a hidden test, the rest of its diff as the solution.
follow.do:
cat > convert.py <<'EOF'
import json, pathlib, subprocess

tickets = json.load(open("tickets.json"))
TEST_SH = """#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Grades one task after the agent has finished. The agent never sees this folder.
set -uo pipefail
TASK="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$1"                                   # the agent's checkout
cp -R "$TASK/tests/hidden/." .            # the PR's own tests, at their real paths, over any edits
status=0
node --test $(cd "$TASK/tests/hidden" && find . -name '*.test.mjs') > /dev/null 2>&1 || status=1
echo "reward $((1 - status))"
"""


def git(*args: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", "product", *args], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout


for line in open("candidates.jsonl"):
    c = json.loads(line)
    t = tickets[c["jira"]]
    task = pathlib.Path("tasks") / f"{c['kind']}-{c['jira']}"
    (task / "tests/hidden").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (task / "solution").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    (task / "instruction.md").write_text(f"# {c['jira']}: {t['summary']}\n\n{t['description']}\n")
    for path in c["hidden_tests"]:
        out = task / "tests/hidden" / path
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out.write_text(git("show", f"{c['merge']}:{path}"))
    (task / "tests/base_sha").write_text(c["base"] + "\n")
    (task / "tests/neighbours").write_text(git("ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", c["base"], "--", "test/"))
    (task / "tests/test.sh").write_text(TEST_SH)
    (task / "solution/fix.patch").write_text(git("diff", c["base"], c["merge"], "--", ".", ":(exclude)test/"))
    print(f"{task}: {', '.join(sorted(str(p.relative_to(task)) for p in task.rglob('*') if p.is_file()))}")
EOF
python3 convert.py
follow.see: tasks/fe_bug-RH-1102: instruction.md, solution/fix.patch, tests/base_sha, tests/hidden/test/title-long.test.mjs, tests/neighbours, tests/test.sh

follow.say: Prove the task both ways, as Harbor's nop and oracle agents would: doing nothing must score 0, the real fix must score 1.
follow.do:
cat > prove.sh <<'EOF'
# Proves one task both ways: doing nothing must score 0, the real fix must score 1.
set -e
TASK="$1"; BASE="$(cat "$TASK/tests/base_sha")"
bash checkout.sh "$BASE" trial-nop
nop=$(bash "$TASK/tests/test.sh" trial-nop)
bash checkout.sh "$BASE" trial-oracle

echo "oracle: $oracle"

EOF

lab.fix: A clever agent noticed that the older test fails and "fixed" it: it changed test/title.test.mjs to call headerTitle("Oncology") without the spaces. Make that edit in trial-agent yourself and grade it again: reward 1, because the grader runs the neighbours from the agent's checkout, edits included. Repair TEST_SH so the neighbours come back from the base commit before they run (git checkout with the base sha and the neighbour paths), the same way the hidden tests are copied over any edits. Then the weakened test makes no difference, and trial-agent scores 0.
explain: Why is the base commit the parent of the squash commit, and what would go wrong if you used the squash commit itself?
A plain clone checked out at the base still leaks the fix. Which refs keep the fix reachable, and what does checkout.sh do to each?
Why must a task score 0 for the nop agent and 1 for the oracle before it joins the bench?
lab.done: One task is mined, cut at its base, proven both ways, and its grader gives 0 to a fix that breaks or weakens an older test.

check.q: After a new skill line, the smoke score jumps from 9 to 13 of 15. One transcript shows Nova copying the merged fix for that very ticket from git history. What is the right next step?

options.text: Ship the skill line, because it raised pass@1 by more than two tasks
options.why: The score measured how well Nova finds answers, not how well it solves tickets. A leaked score is not evidence for anything.

options.text: Close the leak (cut each checkout at the base commit, refuse the source PR in bench mode), then run the bench again before deciding
options.why: Once the answer is out of reach, the bench can say whether the line really helps. It might, but only a clean run can tell.

options.text: Delete the skill line and remove that task from the bench
options.why: The task is fine and the line may be useful. The leak is in how the trials are prepared, and it would affect every task.

check.q: A new task's hidden test passes on the base commit, so Harbor's nop agent scores 1. What does that tell you?

options.text: The task is easy and belongs in the smoke set
options.why: It is not easy, it is empty: a score of 1 for doing nothing means the test does not see the change at all.
The nop agent does nothing, on purpose. The problem is in the task, whose test cannot tell the fixed code from the unfixed code.

options.text: The test does not check what the fix changed, so the task must be repaired or dropped
options.why: Every task must score 0 for nop and 1 for the oracle. Otherwise its score measures nothing about the agent.

check.q: Nova's fix for a task makes the PR's own test pass but breaks an older test next to it. With the grader from this lesson, what does the task score, and why?

options.text: 0, because the grader also runs the neighbours, and a fix that breaks them would never be merged
options.why: The bench should reward fixes a reviewer would accept. Breaking an old test is a regression, whatever the new test says.

options.text: 1, because the hidden test is the only thing that decides the reward
options.why: That is the grader before the Build step. It gave full marks to a fix that broke short names.

options.text: 0.5, because one of two test files passed
options.why: The reward is 1 or 0 for the whole task. Partial credit would make a broken fix look half good.

p: TICKET-BENCH's code is Python in ai-agents/evals/ticket_bench/, in the evals uv project next to a pinned Harbor (G4-02, G4-03). mine.py reads merged fcp PRs from 2025-01-01 to 2026-09-30 with an RH key in the title (about 740 of roughly 1,700 main commits since 2025 carry one), keeps those that change tests and drops the pilot-excluded paths. It writes candidates.jsonl to the restricted golden-set repo, whose name is still to decide. convert.py builds the task folders with git show and git diff. The ticket's task.toml does not match current Harbor (0.24 wants schema_version = "1.4" and a [task] table), so start from harbor init with the pinned version; Python hidden tests also need PYTHONPATH set in test.sh. nova_agent.py runs nova-worker run <task.json> from the harness tarball inside the task environment, in bench mode.

Curation is done with the backend and frontend engineers (G4-10): 40 tasks, nop 0 and oracle 1 for each, 15 marked smoke = true, and tasks/INDEX.md recording kind, size, whether the hidden test reads what the user sees, and who curated it. The ticket's test.sh runs the neighbours from the agent's checkout without restoring them first, so it needs the restore line from this lesson's Fix step. Scoring (G4-25) is score.py, with cost from the gateway's bench:<task>:<try> tag, an evalRun workflow in orchestrator/src/workflows/eval-run.ts on its own eval queue, a required check on harness PRs with no workflow_dispatch, and a monthly schedule that posts the trend to #ai-agents-alerts and the weekly Nova review.

tickets.why: Mining merged PRs into candidates: the filters, the base commit, the kind and the restricted repo.
The Harbor task folder, convert.py, the Nova adapter and bench mode with no leaks.
Curating 40 tasks, proving each one both ways, and grading with the neighbours.
Scores by kind, the smoke gate on harness PRs and the monthly full run.

words.plain: The commit just before a past fix, where the agent starts. With squash merges it is the parent of the fix's commit.
The PR's own tests, kept away from the agent and copied in only when its work is graded.
Any way for the agent to reach the known fix: git history, the source PR, or task data stored where it can read.
Harbor's two check agents: nop does nothing and must score 0, oracle applies the known fix and must score 1.
The tests that existed next to the change before the fix. They must still pass for a reward of 1.
The 15 tasks that run once each on every change to Nova's harness, prompts, skills or image.

review.q: From memory: the four parts a merged PR gives a bench task, and where each one comes from.
review.a: The base commit (the parent of the squash commit), the instruction (the ticket text as people wrote it, up to the merge date), the hidden tests (the PR's test files, from git show at the merge commit), and the solution (the rest of the diff from base to merge, used only by the oracle).

review.q: List the places a past ticket's answer can leak from, and how the bench closes each one.
review.a: Git history in the checkout (cut the checkout at the base: move main, remove the remote, expire the reflog, prune); the broker (in bench mode it refuses the source PR and anything merged after the base); the task data itself (kept in a restricted repo that no agent token covers and the brain never indexes); and Jira comments written after the merge (not mined).

review.q: A harness PR drops the smoke score by one task. Another drops it by two. What does the gate do in each case, and why the difference?
review.a: One task is about 6.7 points on 15 tasks and can be bad luck, so the answer is to run again. Two or more fail the check. A new prompt or skill rule must also raise pass@1 on the full 40 to ship.

remember: A bench task is a past fix turned back in time: start at the base commit with nothing after it, grade with the PR's own tests and the neighbours, and trust a task only after it scores 0 for nothing and 1 for the real fix.
